text:
Elena


Solitary and fearful,

poor helpless vessel,

I wander on the sea of life

in unequal combat.

Why, oh heaven, did you rob me

of sweet maternal shelter?

What shall I be without her dear love

before the fierce gale?


Sad orphan of the world

on the deserted deep,

who in calm weather toward the harbor

will generously guide me?

What pilot among the rocks

that the treacherous sea hides,

from its harmful fury,

ah me, will save me?


If you, benevolent heaven,

deny me daylight,

and hide in shadowy night

the star of salvation;

from disastrous shipwreck

can I free myself, alas sad one,

when the reef that exists

is my own heart?


Oh destiny, be merciful

to the poor abandoned one

who without support, trusting,

gives herself at your mercy.

From the savage storm,

from the mysterious reef,

deliver me, loving heaven,

deliver me, heaven, from myself.

translation.title: The Prayer of a Virgin
translation.editorial_note: The translation follows the extended shipwreck metaphor and treats sana as the likely saña in context.
